Consider the region bounded by the curve $x={y}^{2}-5{y}^{4}$ and the $y$-axis (shown in the picture). Using the shell method, calculate the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated about the $x$-axis. Do not round the answer.

$V=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-5{y}^{4} & =0 \\ {y}^{2}(1-5{y}^{2}) & =0 \\ y & =0\,\text{or}\,{y}^{2}=\frac{1}{5} \\ y & =0\,\text{or}\,y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $y=0$ and $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}yf(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1/\sqrt{5}}y({y}^{2}-5{y}^{4})\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1/\sqrt{5}}({y}^{3}-5{y}^{5})\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi ({\int }_{0}^{1/\sqrt{5}}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y-5{\int }_{0}^{1/\sqrt{5}}{y}^{5}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}\,{|}_{0}^{1/\sqrt{5}}-\frac{5}{6}{y}^{6}\,{|}_{0}^{1/\sqrt{5}}\,) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{1}{4}(\frac{1}{25}-0)-\frac{5}{6}(\frac{1}{125}-0)) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{1}{100}-\frac{1}{150}) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{1}{300}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{150}\end{aligned}
$$
